page: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it features 64 virtual CPUs (32 physical cores with hyperthreading) running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The processor includes a substantial 480 MB L3 cache. Memory configuration consists of 256 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, providing a balanced 4 GB of memory per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data highlights strong computational and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core testing and image processing, alongside exceptional static web serving throughput of 105.74 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is robust, as evidenced by strong ratings in stress-ng multi-core tests, Passmark CPU scores, and bzip3 decompression. The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers strong read-only bandwidth, reaching up to 197.6 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though large-block write bandwidth sits in the average tier. Additionally, the CPU's advanced instruction support, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions), enables strong performance in LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing on large 70B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m8i-flex.16xlarge offers a balanced resource density suitable for workloads requiring high-frequency compute and modern memory architectures without the premium of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The absence of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled, allowing users to scale EBS volumes independently. This profile is highly suited for enterprise applications, static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
